line: What was the best part of your day?
followUps: What made that part good?
What was the rest of it like?
shareBack: Offer the best part of your own day in a sentence, then ask what tomorrow looks like.

line: You've seemed a little weighed down this week. I'm around whenever you want to talk it through.
followUps: What's been the heaviest part?
Do you want ideas, or just someone to listen?
shareBack: Mention one thing that has weighed on you lately, briefly, then hand the turn back.
deliveryCue: Only if you've noticed it. Then listen; don't fix.

line: What's taking up the most room in your head this week?
followUps: What's the hardest part of that?
What would make it feel lighter?
shareBack: Once they have finished, offer what is filling your own head in a sentence, then ask what would help.
deliveryCue: Listen; don't fix unless they ask.

line: You were great with everyone tonight. Who did you enjoy talking to most?
followUps: What did you two get into?
Anyone you wish you'd had longer with?
shareBack: Mention the conversation you enjoyed most, then ask who you should both see again soon.

line: Anything you want us to make time for this weekend?
followUps: What would make that easy to fit in?
Just us, or with other people?
shareBack: Offer one thing you'd like to fit in too, then ask which should come first.

line: What are you looking forward to most in the next few weeks?
followUps: What's the best part of that for you?
Is there anything I can do to help it happen?
shareBack: Offer one thing you're looking forward to, then ask what they'd add to the calendar.

line: Something's been stuck in my head today. Can I think out loud for a minute, then hear what's on yours?
followUps: What's been on yours?
What part of that bothers you most?
shareBack: Keep your part to a minute, then give them the longer turn.
deliveryCue: When it's their turn, listen; don't fix.

line: Is there anything coming up that you'd like more help with from me?
followUps: What would that look like day to day?
What's the first thing I could take on?
shareBack: Mention one thing you could use a hand with too, then agree on one small change.
deliveryCue: Take the answer as given; don't defend.

line: I'm glad we came. Give me a look if you need rescuing from anyone.
followUps: Who have you enjoyed catching up with?
How long would you like to stay?
shareBack: Mention who you've enjoyed talking to, then ask who you should both go and find.

line: Who are you hoping to catch up with while we're here?
followUps: What do you want to ask them about?
Anyone you'd rather we tackled together?
shareBack: Mention who you want to see, then ask who you should find first.

line: I was thinking about that trip we took a while back. What's the part you still think about?
followUps: What made that part stick?
Where should we go next?
shareBack: Offer the moment you remember best, in a sentence, then ask what they'd do again.
deliveryCue: Let them tell it their way; don't correct the details.

line: Thinking of you. No need to reply, I just hope the afternoon's going okay.
followUps: What was the afternoon like in the end?
What would make tonight easy?
shareBack: Tonight, mention one small thing from your own afternoon, then ask about theirs.

line: What sounds good for dinner tonight? I can pick something up on the way.
followUps: Anything else you need while I'm out?
Eat at the table or in front of a show?
shareBack: Offer what you're in the mood for, then let them choose.

line: Good luck with the big thing today. I want to hear all about it tonight.
followUps: How did it go?
What part went better than you expected?
shareBack: After they have told it all, mention one thing from your day, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: Tonight, ask and listen; don't fix.

line: Thanks for this morning. It made my day easier. What can I take off your plate tonight?
followUps: What else is on the list this week?
What would you rather do with that time?
shareBack: Mention one thing you'd like help with this week too, then settle who does what.

line: Just saw something that made me think of you. Remind me to tell you tonight.
followUps: What made you laugh today?
What was the oddest part of your day?
shareBack: Tell the story in a few sentences tonight, then ask for one from their day.

line: Want to do something just us this weekend? You pick.
followUps: What would make it feel like a real break?
Which day suits you better?
shareBack: Offer one idea of your own as a backup, then go with their choice.

line: Is there something you've been wanting us to do differently lately?
followUps: What would that look like in a normal week?
What's one small step we could try first?
shareBack: Once they have finished, offer one thing you'd like to change too, then pick one to try.
deliveryCue: Listen all the way through before you answer.

line: I don't say it enough, but I see how much you carry for us. Which part is heaviest right now?
followUps: What would take some of that off you?
When did it start feeling like that?
shareBack: Mention one thing you find heavy too, briefly, then return to what they need.
deliveryCue: Thank them first; don't explain or defend.

line: I've never heard the full story of how I got my name. How did you land on it?
followUps: Who else had a say in it?
What other names were on the list?
shareBack: Mention how you feel about your name now, then ask about another family name.

line: What was this holiday like when you were a kid?
followUps: Who did the cooking back then?
Which part of it do you miss most?
shareBack: Offer your own earliest memory of this holiday, then ask what they'd bring back.

line: I tried making one of your dishes and it wasn't the same. What's the trick?
followUps: Who taught you to make it?
What else should I learn while I'm at it?
shareBack: Mention how your attempt turned out, then ask which dish to try next.

line: What was your first job like?
followUps: What did you spend your first pay on?
Who do you still remember from there?
shareBack: Offer one detail about your own first job, then ask what they did next.

line: What was the house you grew up in like?
followUps: Which room do you remember best?
Who else lived there with you?
shareBack: Mention one thing you remember about your own childhood home, then ask about the street.

line: Who in the family am I most like, do you think?
followUps: What do I do that reminds you of them?
What were they like at my age?
shareBack: Mention who you think you take after, then ask who they take after.

line: What's a family story I've probably never heard?
followUps: Who told you that one?
What happened afterwards?
shareBack: Offer a short family story you love, then ask if they remember it the same way.

line: I've got a decision I keep going back and forth on. Can I get your take?
followUps: What would you want to know before deciding?
Did you ever face something like this?
shareBack: Lay the choice out in two sentences, then listen to the whole answer before replying.

line: What are you reading or watching at the moment? I need something new.
followUps: What do you like about it?
What should I try after that?
shareBack: Offer one thing you've enjoyed lately, then ask what they'd pick next.

line: What's been the best part of your week so far?
followUps: What made that stand out?
What's the rest of the week looking like?
shareBack: Offer the best part of your own week in a sentence, then ask about the weekend.

line: I caught myself doing something exactly the way you do it this week. Where did you learn it?
followUps: Who taught you that?
What else did you pick up from them?
shareBack: Say what the habit was and when you noticed it, then ask what else they taught you.

line: It's really good to see you. I've thought about you more than I've managed to say.
followUps: What's been keeping you busy lately?
What's been good for you this year?
shareBack: Mention one thing from your own year in a sentence, then ask another question about theirs.

line: I was thinking the other day about the meals at your place when I was small. What do you remember from then?
followUps: Who was always at the table?
What did you like cooking most?
shareBack: Offer the one dish or moment you remember best, then ask what else you've forgotten.

line: This must bring back some memories. What were family get-togethers like when you were young?
followUps: Who was always the life of the room?
What did everyone eat?
shareBack: Mention a gathering you remember from childhood, then ask how today compares.

line: What are you proud of that nobody really asks you about?
followUps: What did it take to do that?
Who knew about it at the time?
shareBack: Tell them one thing about them that you're proud of, then ask what came next.

line: Is there anything you'd do differently if you were my age again?
followUps: What made you choose the way you did?
What are you glad you didn't change?
shareBack: Mention one choice you're weighing now, briefly, then ask what they'd tell you.

line: I was telling someone about what we got up to as kids. What's your favorite story from back then?
followUps: Do you remember how it started?
Who got the blame?
shareBack: Offer the story you tell most, in a few sentences, then ask if you've got it right.

line: What have you been spending your spare time on lately?
followUps: How did you get into that?
What do you like most about it?
shareBack: Offer one thing that has been filling your own spare time, then ask what's next for theirs.

line: This is a serious spread. Which dish do you go for first?
followUps: Is there one you look forward to every year?
Who made the best thing here?
shareBack: Mention the dish you're heading for, then ask what you shouldn't miss.

line: It's been forever since this many of us were in one room. Who have you caught up with so far?
followUps: Who were you most glad to see?
Who should I go and find?
shareBack: Mention who you've talked to so far, then ask who you should say hello to next.

line: How was the trip over? Did you come far today?
followUps: What time did you have to leave?
Are you staying on or heading back tonight?
shareBack: Mention your own trip in a sentence, then ask what they're looking forward to today.

line: You're always the one who gets everyone laughing at these things. Where do you get it from?
followUps: Who was the funny one when you were growing up?
What's the best laugh you've had today?
shareBack: Mention one thing they said that you still quote, then ask for another story.

line: I heard a song this week that took me straight back to being a kid. What does that for you?
followUps: Where does it take you back to?
Who were you with back then?
shareBack: Say which song it was and where it took you, in a sentence, then ask about theirs.

line: You've seemed stretched thin lately. I'd like to hear what's going on whenever you've got the energy.
followUps: What's taking the most out of you?
What would help this week?
shareBack: Mention one thing that has stretched you lately, briefly, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: Only if you've noticed it. Listen; don't jump in with fixes.

line: What's been the highlight of your year so far?
followUps: What made it so good?
What are you hoping the rest of the year brings?
shareBack: Offer your own highlight in a sentence, then ask what's coming up next.

line: What's something you've found lately that you'd recommend to everyone?
followUps: How did you come across it?
What would I like about it?
shareBack: Offer one recommendation of your own, then ask for a second.

line: What are you cooking these days? I'm stuck in a rut and need ideas.
followUps: How do you make it?
What's your easy weeknight one?
shareBack: Mention the one meal you make too often, then ask what they'd swap it for.

line: Do you have any trips or plans lined up for the next few months?
followUps: What are you most looking forward to about it?
How did that come about?
shareBack: Offer one plan of your own, then ask what else is on their list.

line: Do you think we turned out the way the family expected?
followUps: What did they expect of you?
What surprised you most about how things went?
shareBack: Offer how you think you turned out, in a sentence, then ask what they'd tell their younger self.

line: I've heard so much about your cooking. What's the dish everyone asks you for?
followUps: Who did you learn it from?
When do you usually make it?
shareBack: Mention a dish from your own family table, then ask what they like to eat when someone else cooks.

line: What does this holiday usually look like in your family? I'd love to know the traditions.
followUps: Which tradition is your favorite?
How long has the family done that?
shareBack: Offer one tradition from your side, then ask which of theirs you should learn first.

line: What a lovely day for it. Which part have you enjoyed most so far?
followUps: What are you looking forward to next?
Who have you managed to catch up with?
shareBack: Mention the moment you liked best, then ask about the people they came to see.

line: Your place is lovely. How long have you lived here?
followUps: What do you like best about living here?
What was it like when you first moved in?
shareBack: Mention one thing you like about the house or the street, then ask about their favorite spot.

line: I'd love a story from when my other half was little. Which one always gets told?
followUps: What were they like at that age?
Who else was in on it?
shareBack: Offer one childhood story of your own, briefly, then ask for another of theirs.

line: What's the area like around where you live? I've never spent much time there.
followUps: What do you like best about it?
Where would you take a visitor first?
shareBack: Mention one thing you like about where you live, then ask how long they've been there.

line: What should I make sure I see or eat while I'm in your part of the world?
followUps: Where do you go yourself?
What do visitors usually miss?
shareBack: Mention one place you've liked so far, then ask where they'd spend a free afternoon.

line: What was the house like when the whole family lived under one roof?
followUps: Who was the noisy one?
What did a normal weekend look like?
shareBack: Offer one detail about the home you grew up in, then ask what they miss about those years.

line: Thank you for having us. You make it look easy. What can I do to help?
followUps: How long have you been hosting this one?
What's the part you enjoy most?
shareBack: Mention one thing you're enjoying about the day, then get stuck into the job they give you.

line: Is there a dish that has to be on the table every year?
followUps: Who makes it?
What happens if someone tries to change it?
shareBack: Mention the dish your own family insists on, then ask how theirs is made.

line: How did the family traditions start? Was it your side, or something you made up along the way?
followUps: Which one matters most to you?
Has it changed much over the years?
shareBack: Offer one tradition you'd like to keep going, then ask how you can help with theirs.

line: The hosts have done a wonderful job. Have you had a chance to talk to them yet?
followUps: What's been your favorite part so far?
Who else are you hoping to see?
shareBack: Mention one detail of the day you liked, then ask what they thought of the food.

line: Made your recipe tonight and thought of you. It came out nearly right.
followUps: What do you think I got wrong?
What should I try next?
shareBack: Say how it turned out in a line, then ask when you can cook it together.

line: Are you free for a call this weekend? Nothing urgent, I'd just like to hear your voice.
followUps: Which day suits you best?
What's been happening at your place this week?
shareBack: On the call, offer one small piece of your own news, then ask for theirs.

line: Saw something today that reminded me of you and it made me smile. No need to reply. Hope you're well.
followUps: What have you been up to this year?
Would a call sometime suit you?
shareBack: If they reply, mention the memory in a line, then ask one easy question about them.

line: It's been too long, and that's on me. I'd love to catch up whenever suits you. No rush at all.
followUps: When's a good time for a call?
What's been the best part of your year?
shareBack: If they reply, offer one line of your own news, then ask about theirs.

line: Found an old photo of us today and had to send it. Hope things are good with you.
followUps: Do you remember where this was taken?
Who else was there that day?
shareBack: If they reply, mention what you remember of that day, then ask what they remember.

line: I'm making soup tonight and it's missing something. What would you add?
followUps: How long do you let it cook?
What do you serve with it?
shareBack: Reply with how it turned out, then ask what they're cooking this week.

line: What's the weather doing where you are today? It's been wild here.
followUps: Have you managed to get out in it?
What do you have planned for the rest of the day?
shareBack: Mention one line about your own day, then ask what they're up to this week.

line: I've been thinking about the stories you used to tell. Can I ask you about one next time I'm over?
followUps: Which story do you like telling most?
Is there one you've never told me?
shareBack: Mention the story you remember best in a line, then let them pick where to start.

line: Here's a photo from today. I thought you might like to have it.
followUps: What was your favorite part of the day?
Shall I send the rest?
shareBack: Mention the moment you liked best, in a line, then ask about theirs.

line: Really good to see you the other day. Let's not leave it so long next time.
followUps: When are you next around?
What do you have going on over the next few weeks?
shareBack: Offer a rough date that suits you, then ask what works for them.

line: What was the name of that show you mentioned? I want to try it.
followUps: When does it get good?
What else are you enjoying?
shareBack: Reply once you've watched some with what you liked, then ask what to watch next.

line: Are you going to the family get-together next month? It'd be good to see you there.
followUps: Are you staying over or just there for the day?
Is there anything I can bring?
shareBack: Mention when you're arriving, then ask who else is coming.

line: Can I pick your brain about something this week? You're the person I thought of first.
followUps: When's a good time to call?
How did you learn so much about this?
shareBack: Give the question in two lines so they can think ahead, then thank them for the time.

line: Settle something for me: what was the name of that place we always went as kids?
followUps: What do you remember most about it?
Should we go back sometime?
shareBack: Mention what you remember of it in a line, then ask what else you've forgotten.

line: It was lovely to meet you over the weekend. Thank you for making me feel so welcome.
followUps: Is there anything I can bring next time?
What do you have planned for the week?
shareBack: Mention one moment you enjoyed, in a line, then say you hope to see them again soon.

line: Thank you again for dinner. I'm still thinking about that dessert. Any chance of the recipe?
followUps: Where did the recipe come from?
What do you usually serve with it?
shareBack: Reply with how your attempt turned out, then ask what they'd like you to cook for them.

line: We got home safely. Thank you for a lovely day.
followUps: What was your favorite part of the day?
When can we have you over to ours?
shareBack: Mention the moment you enjoyed most, in a line, then suggest when you'll next see them.

line: Is there anything we can bring next time we come over?
followUps: What does everyone like to drink?
Would it help if we came early to set up?
shareBack: Offer one thing you'd be glad to make or bring, then let them choose.

line: I loved hearing your stories over the weekend. I'd like to hear more next time.
followUps: Which story should I ask for next?
Are there photos to go with them?
shareBack: Mention the story that stayed with you, in a line, then say when you'll next visit.

line: I'm making a snack. Want one?
followUps: Sweet or savoury?
Want to eat it in here or take it with you?
shareBack: Mention one small thing from your day while you cook, then leave space.
deliveryCue: Say it in passing and carry on; let them come to you.

line: You pick the music. I want to hear what you're into at the moment.
followUps: What do you like about this one?
Who introduced you to them?
shareBack: Mention one song you loved at their age, briefly, then let the music play.
deliveryCue: Eyes on the road, and no comments on their taste.

line: Saw this and thought of you. No need to reply.
followUps: What's the funniest thing you've seen this week?
Got one to send back?
shareBack: If they answer, reply with one line or an emoji, not a question about school.
deliveryCue: Send it with the picture or clip and leave it there.

line: Proud of you for today. That's all.
followUps: What part are you happiest with?
What do you want to do to celebrate?
shareBack: Later, mention the exact thing you noticed them do, then let them take it from there.
deliveryCue: Send it and leave it; no question straight after.

line: Getting food on my way home. Want anything?
followUps: Same as last time?
Anything for later as well?
shareBack: Say what you're getting for yourself, then eat together if they're up for it.
deliveryCue: A yes or no is a full answer; don't push for more.

line: Good luck today. I'm around later if you want to tell me about it.
followUps: Which part went best?
What do you need tonight?
shareBack: If they bring it up, mention a time you were nervous before something, in a sentence.
deliveryCue: Wait for them to raise it tonight; don't open with a question.

line: Sorry I was short this morning. That was about me, not you.
followUps: Is there anything you wanted to say that I cut off?
Can we start over tonight?
shareBack: Tonight, say in one sentence what was going on for you, then let them respond or not.
deliveryCue: Don't add 'but'. Send it and let it land.

line: Drive-through run tonight? My treat.
followUps: Where do you want to go?
Want to bring anyone?
shareBack: In the car, mention one small thing from your day, then let them pick the music.
deliveryCue: Keep it an offer; no agenda once you're in the car.

line: I had a weird day. Want to hear the dumbest part?
followUps: Has anything like that happened to you?
What would you have done?
shareBack: Keep your story under a minute, then leave room for one of theirs.

line: I need your opinion on something. Which of these would you pick?
followUps: What makes that one better?
What would you change about it?
shareBack: Say which one you were leaning toward, then go with theirs if you can.
deliveryCue: Ask about something real, and take the answer seriously.

line: If you want a break from the table, I could use a hand in the kitchen.
followUps: Who have you ended up stuck next to?
Want to be in charge of dessert?
shareBack: Mention who you find hard work at these things, quietly, then share the job.
deliveryCue: Say it quietly, as a way out, not a chore.

line: What are you watching lately that I'd actually like?
followUps: What's it about, without spoilers?
Can we watch the first one together?
shareBack: Mention one show you're in the middle of, then let them choose what goes on.
deliveryCue: One question, then stop. Follow up only if they light up.

line: You don't have to talk to everyone today. Give me a look if you need rescuing.
followUps: Who are you actually glad to see?
What would make today easier?
shareBack: Mention who you'd like rescuing from, then agree on a signal.
deliveryCue: Say it on the way there or early on, just the two of you.

line: You seem worn out this week. I'm not going to quiz you. I'm here if you want to talk.
followUps: Do you want ideas, or just someone to listen?
What would make this week easier?
shareBack: If they open up, mention one time you felt the same, in a sentence, then go back to them.
deliveryCue: Only if you've noticed it. Say it once, then leave a long pause.

line: Can you show me how this works? I keep getting it wrong.
followUps: How did you work that out?
What else can it do?
shareBack: Mention what you were trying to do with it, then let them drive.
deliveryCue: Hand over the phone or controller and let them be the expert.

followUps: What are the options?
What should we definitely not watch?
shareBack: Offer one movie you'd veto, then back their choice in front of everyone.

line: When I was your age I worried a lot about fitting in. I don't know if it's like that for you.
followUps: What's it like with your friends at the moment?
What do you wish adults understood about it?
shareBack: Offer one short, true story from that age, then let them decide whether to add theirs.

line: What was the funniest thing that happened today?
followUps: What happened next?
Who else was laughing?
shareBack: Tell them one funny thing from your own day, then ask if anything else made them laugh.
deliveryCue: Try at bedtime or one-on-one, not the moment you see them.

line: Who did you sit with at lunch today?
followUps: What did you two talk about?
What did you have to eat?
shareBack: Mention who you had lunch with, then ask who they'd like to sit with tomorrow.
deliveryCue: Ask after a snack, once they've had a few quiet minutes.

line: What was the hardest part of today?
followUps: What did you do when that happened?
What would help next time?
shareBack: Mention one small hard thing from your day and what you did, then give them a hug.
deliveryCue: Bedtime, lights low. Listen; don't fix it.

line: What was your favorite part of practice today?
followUps: What made that part fun?
What do you want to try next time?
shareBack: Mention the part you most enjoyed watching, then ask what they'd like for a snack.
deliveryCue: Ask on the walk to the car, not in front of the others.

line: I loved watching you keep trying out there. Which part felt best?
followUps: What were you thinking when you did that?
What do you want to show me next time?
shareBack: Mention the exact moment you noticed, then let them tell you about it.
deliveryCue: Praise the effort, not the score. Say it right after.

line: I'm so glad I got to watch you today.
followUps: What was the most fun part?
Who were you playing with?
shareBack: Mention one thing you liked seeing, then let them choose what to talk about.
deliveryCue: Say it and stop; no coaching on the way home.

line: Who made you laugh today?
followUps: What did they do?
What did you do then?
shareBack: Tell them who made you laugh today, then ask who they want to play with tomorrow.
deliveryCue: Good in the car or while you're doing something side by side.

line: What's your favorite thing on the table?
followUps: What does it taste like?
What should we try next?
shareBack: Point out your own favorite, then ask which one they'd like to help make next year.
deliveryCue: Ask quietly, beside them, not across the table.

line: Who do you want to play with after we eat?
followUps: What game will you play?
Can anyone join in?
shareBack: Mention who you're looking forward to talking to, then ask what they need for the game.
deliveryCue: Ask before the meal, down at their level.

line: What are you most excited about today?
followUps: What do you think it will be like?
What do you want to do first?
shareBack: Tell them the one thing you're excited about, then ask how you can help with theirs.
deliveryCue: Ask at breakfast or in the car on the way.

line: I need a helper. Do you want to stir or set the table?
followUps: How should we do it?
What should we do next?
shareBack: Tell them what you used to help with at their age, then ask what job they'd like next.
deliveryCue: Give two choices and let them pick; chat while you work.

line: Show me what you made today. I want to hear how you did it.
followUps: Which part took the longest?
What will you make next?
shareBack: Point to the one detail you like best, then ask where it should go.
deliveryCue: Get down to their level and look properly before you speak.

line: I can't decide what to read tonight. Which book should we pick?
followUps: What do you like about that one?
Which part should I do the voices for?
shareBack: Mention a book you loved when you were small, then start reading theirs.
deliveryCue: Ask at bedtime, once teeth are done.

line: You were so patient at the table. What was the best part of dinner?
followUps: Who did you like talking to?
What should we have next time?
shareBack: Tell them your best part, then ask what they want to do now.
deliveryCue: Say it afterwards, just the two of you.
